systemOverview.title: System overview

intro.title: Welcome to AviSafe
intro.description: We'll walk you through the main menu so you know where everything is. Use Next, Back or Skip at any time.

nav-missions.title: Missions
nav-missions.description: Plan, run and document all drone operations here. This is the heart of the workflow.

nav-map.title: Map
nav-map.description: View airspace, NOTAMs, weather and plan routes. Used for planning and operational assessment.

nav-documents.title: Documents
nav-documents.description: Shared document library for procedures, manuals and reports.

nav-calendar.title: Calendar
nav-calendar.description: Get an overview of planned missions and scheduling.

nav-incidents.title: Incidents
nav-incidents.description: Report deviations, observations and incidents. Important for continuous safety.

nav-status.title: Status
nav-status.description: Operational status for the company — ongoing flights and alerts.

nav-resources.title: Resources
nav-resources.description: Drones, batteries, equipment, maintenance, personnel and competencies.

nav-changelog.title: System status
nav-changelog.description: View the changelog and operational messages for the platform.

nav-admin.title: Administration
nav-admin.description: Company settings, user management and integrations. Only visible to administrators.

nav-profile.title: My profile
nav-profile.description: Personal information, security, competencies and notifications. You can restart this guide from here.

finish.title: That was the main menu!
finish.description: You'll find all modules from the top. Tip: Start the "Create mission" guide when you're ready to learn the mission workflow.

dashboardWidgets.title: The dashboard widgets
dashboardWidgets.description: Get to know the widgets on the home page — what they show and how to use them.

intro.title: Welcome to the dashboard
intro.description: The home page gives you a quick overview: active flights, news, status, missions, incidents, calendar and KPIs. You can drag the widgets to change the order.

log-flight.title: Log flight time / Upload flight log
log-flight.description: Register flight time manually after an operation, or upload a flight log from DJI/ArduPilot for automatic parsing of telemetry, battery and flight path.

flight-controls.title: Start / end flight
flight-controls.description: Start a flight to activate the timer, checklists and live position (DroneTag). Press "End" when you land — the duration is saved and you can complete the post-flight checklist.

active-flights.title: Active flights
active-flights.description: Shows ongoing flights in real time for your company — pilot, drone, duration and position. Click a flight to follow it on the map.

ai-search.title: AI search
ai-search.description: Ask AviSafe in natural language — e.g. "show latest missions in Oslo" or "which drones need maintenance?". The AI searches across the modules you have access to.

news.title: News
news.description: Operational messages, new features and alerts from AviSafe and your company. Keep an eye on this for important updates.

status.title: Status
status.description: Status overview of your resources — drones, batteries and equipment approaching or overdue for maintenance, plus personnel with competencies expiring soon or expired.

missions.title: Missions
missions.description: Your upcoming and ongoing missions. Click a mission to open the planner, checklists and documentation.

calendar.title: Calendar
calendar.description: Overview of planned missions this and next week. Click a date to open the full calendar.

incidents.title: Incidents
incidents.description: Latest reported incidents and deviations. Follow up open cases or register new ones to keep safety work moving.

documents.title: Documents
documents.description: Shortcut to the latest documents — manuals, checklists and procedures. Click to open the document library.

kpi.title: KPIs
kpi.description: Charts and figures showing flight time, number of missions and incidents over time — useful for management and reporting.

finish.title: That was the widgets!
finish.description: Tip: Drag and drop the widgets to customize your dashboard. You can start this guide again from the profile page.

incidentReport.title: Reporting incidents
incidentReport.description: Learn how to quickly report an incident from the dashboard widget, and how to find a full overview on the Incidents page.

widget-intro.title: Incident widget
widget-intro.description: The incident widget on the dashboard gives a quick overview of the latest reports and a shortcut to report something new.

widget-report.title: Report incident
widget-report.description: Click here to open the report form directly. Quick access is important — the threshold for reporting should be low.

widget-tabs.title: Incidents and follow-up
widget-tabs.description: If you are a follow-up owner you get a dedicated "Follow-up" tab with cases assigned to you, so nothing falls through the cracks.

widget-list.title: Click for details
widget-list.description: Click a card to open the detail dialog with comments, attachments, ECCAIRS status and links to missions/resources.

open-dialog.title: Report form
open-dialog.description: This is the same form whether you open it from the widget or from the Incidents page. We'll go through the fields from top to bottom.

mission.title: Link to mission
mission.description: Select a mission to pre-fill pilot, drone, location and time — and to give full traceability between the incident and the operation.

title-desc.title: Title and description
title-desc.description: Title is required. Describe what happened, where and why — the more context, the better the learning afterwards.

meta.title: Time, severity and status
meta.description: Set the time of the incident and choose severity (Low/Medium/High/Critical). "Critical" triggers a notification to admin.

classification.title: Classification
classification.description: Category, primary cause and contributing causes are used in statistics and for ECCAIRS reporting to the Civil Aviation Authority.

resources.title: Resources (drone, pilot, equipment)
resources.description: Link resources so the incident automatically appears in the logbook of each drone/equipment unit — important for maintenance and analysis.

image.title: Image
image.description: Attach an image directly. More attachments can be added in the detail dialog after the incident is created.

followup.title: Follow-up owner
followup.description: Assign an owner — they'll receive a notification and see the case in their "Follow-up" tab on the dashboard.

anonymous.title: Anonymous reporting
anonymous.description: You can choose to report anonymously. Admin can also enable a company setting that makes all reports anonymous automatically.

submit.title: Submit the report
submit.description: Press Report to save. We'll move on to the Incidents page to see where you find the full overview.

nav.title: Go to Incidents
nav.description: On the Incidents page you get a full overview with search, filtering, ECCAIRS reporting, attachments and PDF export.

search.title: Search
search.description: Search title, description, mission and location across all incidents you have access to.

status-filter.title: Status filter
status-filter.description: Filter by Open, In progress, Resolved or Closed to focus on what requires action.

add.title: New incident
add.description: Same report form as from the widget. Use this when you're already on the Incidents page.

outro.title: Done
outro.description: Now you know how to report and find incidents again. You can restart this tour from My profile → Competencies.

logFlight.title: Log flight time / end flight
logFlight.description: Learn how to log flight time manually or end an active flight. The same dialog is used in both cases.

intro.title: End flight or log manually
intro.description: When you stop an active flight, this dialog opens automatically and fills in time, drone and pilot. You can also open it manually to log a flight afterwards — we'll show the latter now.

open-dialog.title: Log flight time dialog
open-dialog.description: Here you register flight time, departure and landing location, drone, pilot, equipment and movements. Data is saved in the flight log and updates the drone's flight time.

mission.title: Link mission
mission.description: Link the flight time to a mission for traceability. Once a mission is selected you can set it to "Completed" directly from here.

drone.title: Select drone
drone.description: Select the drone that was used. Drone time and number of movements are automatically updated on the resource for maintenance tracking.

pilot.title: Pilot
pilot.description: Select pilot — this gives correct logging per pilot, and is used in the competency/experience overview.

times.title: Date, location and duration
times.description: Fill in date, departure and landing location, and duration (minutes or from/to time). Duration and hours are calculated automatically.

movements.title: Movements and operation type
movements.description: Number of landings and operation type (VLOS / BVLOS / EVLOS). Included in statistics and important for regulatory reporting.

submit.title: Save flight time
submit.description: Press "Log flight time" to save. The log is shown on the Statistics page and updates the drone's maintenance status.

missionCreation.title: Create mission (map flow)
missionCreation.description: Recommended workflow: plan the route on the map with SORA buffer and adjacent areas, and save — the mission dialog opens pre-filled.

kart-intro.title: Start on the map
kart-intro.description: AviSafe's recommended workflow for new missions is to start on the map. This gets the route, SORA volume, population and airspace right from the start.

start-route-planner.title: Plan new route
start-route-planner.description: Click "Plan new route" (the route icon) to open the route planner. Here you draw the operation area directly on the map.

draw-route.title: Draw the route on the map
draw-route.description: Click on the map to add route points. At least 3 points for an area, 2 for a corridor. Once you have at least 2 points, the "Save" button becomes active. Click "Next" when you're ready.

sora-toggle.title: Enable SORA volume
sora-toggle.description: Enable "SORA volume" to calculate flight geometry, contingency and ground risk buffer. Select drone, speed and altitude in the panel — values are filled in automatically from the drone model.

adjacent-toggle.title: Adjacent areas
adjacent-toggle.description: Enable "Adjacent" to calculate population density around the operation. This gives you required containment, SAIL and documentation for the risk assessment.

pilot-position.title: Place pilot (optional)
pilot-position.description: Click "Pilot" and then on the map to mark the pilot position. Used for VLOS check and documentation.

kml-import.title: Import KML/KMZ
kml-import.description: Upload a KML or KMZ file (e.g. exported from DJI Pilot, Google Earth or other tools) to fill in the route automatically instead of drawing manually.

ippc-link.title: IPPC – check NOTAM
ippc-link.description: Opens ippc.no in a new tab so you can check active NOTAMs for the area before you fly. Remember to consider relevant NOTAMs as part of the risk assessment.

sensor-link.title: Sensor – NSM application
sensor-link.description: Opens the NSM portal for applying to fly with a sensor in sensor-prohibited zones. Use this if your route touches such a zone.

fh2-send.title: Send to DJI FlightHub 2
fh2-send.description: Visible if the company has connected a FlightHub 2 token and the route has at least 2 points. Sends the route and SORA corridor directly to FH2 as a task for the pilot.

undo-point.title: Undo last point
undo-point.description: Removes the last placed route point. Use this if you clicked wrong — the route updates immediately.

clear-route.title: Clear route
clear-route.description: Deletes all route points, but keeps the route planner open so you can start over without closing the panel.

cancel-route.title: Cancel route planning
cancel-route.description: Closes the route planner and discards the current route without saving. Use this if you decide not to create a mission after all.

save-route.title: Save the route
save-route.description: Click "Save" when the route and buffer are ready. The mission dialog now opens pre-filled with route, SORA data, drone and buffer — you only need to fill in name, customer, time and personnel.

finish.title: You're ready!
finish.description: After saving, fill in the rest in the mission dialog and publish. You can restart this guide from My profile → Competencies, or the help button at the top.

resources.title: Resources — drones, equipment and personnel
resources.description: In-depth walkthrough of the entire Resources module. We go thoroughly through all three sections and dive into the dialogs for editing, logbook and competencies.

intro.title: Welcome to Resources
intro.description: Here you keep track of the entire fleet: your drones/aircraft, the equipment attached to them, and personnel with competencies. The page is split into three columns — we'll go through each of them.

drone-section.title: Drones / aircraft
drone-section.description: The first column shows all drones/aircraft available to your company — including those shared from a parent company.

drone-add.title: Add new drone
drone-add.description: Press "+" to register a new drone. You can select from the drone catalog (M4D, M400 etc.) — weight, payload and class will then be filled in automatically.

drone-search.title: Search drones
drone-search.description: Search by model name, registration number or serial number. Results update as you type.

drone-filters.title: Filters and sorting
drone-filters.description: Filter by model and status (green/yellow/red), or sort by "Last flown" to find the drone you used last.

drone-card.title: Drone card
drone-card.description: Each card shows model, pilot, registration number, last flown, total flight hours and next inspection. The status color at the top right summarizes maintenance + warnings.

drone-detail.title: Drone details
drone-detail.description: Click a card to open the detail view. Here you see all technical info: model, serial number, class, weight, payload, purchase date, next inspection, connected equipment and personnel.

drone-detail-logbok.title: Open the logbook
drone-detail-logbok.description: The logbook button shows the drone's full history: all flights, maintenance, inspections, incidents and notes.

drone-logbook.title: The logbook
drone-logbook.description: The logbook collects all events chronologically: missions (auto-generated from completed missions), manual flight time, maintenance entries, incidents and notes.

drone-logbook-add.title: Add entry
drone-logbook-add.description: Here you manually register a note, incident, repair or similar. You can attach an image, link to a drone and set a date.

drone-logbook-export.title: Export to PDF
drone-logbook-export.description: Export the entire logbook as a PDF — it is also saved under "Documents" on the drone, so you have a versioned paper trail for authorities or audits.

drone-detail-back.title: Back to drone
drone-detail-back.description: We close the logbook and are back in the drone details. Here you can also register maintenance/inspection performed, attach equipment, link personnel and change associated checklists.

drone-detail-edit.title: Edit drone
drone-detail-edit.description: Press "Edit" to change model, serial number, class, weight, payload, internal serial, registration number, status, maintenance/inspection intervals and associated checklists.

add-drone.title: Register new drone
add-drone.description: Select a model from the drone catalog and weight, payload, class and notes are filled in automatically — or select "Enter manually". Set serial number, internal serial and purchase date.

add-drone-inspection.title: Inspection plan
add-drone-inspection.description: Set the inspection start date and interval (days) to automatically calculate the next inspection date. Select the checklist that must be completed before the inspection can be signed off.

equipment-section.title: Equipment
equipment-section.description: The second column is equipment — cameras, gimbals, batteries, sensors and other items. You can also add DroneTag devices (Remote ID).

equipment-add.title: Add equipment
equipment-add.description: Register a new piece of equipment: name, type, serial number, weight and maintenance rules (days / flight hours / number of missions).

equipment-dronetag.title: DroneTag
equipment-dronetag.description: Dedicated button for DroneTag devices (live positioning / Remote ID). These also appear in the list and can be linked to a drone for "Live UAV".

equipment-filters.title: Search and filters
equipment-filters.description: Filter by category and status, or search by name, type, serial number or note.

equipment-card.title: Equipment card
equipment-card.description: Each card shows type, serial number, next maintenance and status. Press it to open the detail view.

equipment-detail.title: Equipment details
equipment-detail.description: The detail view for equipment shows name, type, serial numbers, weight, total flight hours, status, warnings and which drones it is mounted on.

equipment-detail-logbok.title: Equipment logbook
equipment-detail-logbok.description: The logbook button shows incidents, maintenance and repairs for this equipment — regardless of which drone it was mounted on.

equipment-logbook.title: Equipment logbook
equipment-logbook.description: Same setup as the drone logbook: add entries, attach images, export PDF. Flight hours accumulate automatically each time the equipment is included in a completed mission.

add-equipment.title: Register new equipment
add-equipment.description: Set name, type/category, serial number and weight. Maintenance can be tracked by days, flight hours or number of missions — set warning thresholds to get a yellow light before it's overdue.

add-dronetag.title: Add DroneTag
add-dronetag.description: DroneTag devices require you to enter a device ID. After registration, the device can be linked to a drone and used for live positioning during flight.

personnel-section.title: Personnel
personnel-section.description: The third column shows personnel in the company (and personnel shared from parent/child companies). Each person has a competency list with expiry dates and status.

personnel-add.title: Add competency
personnel-add.description: The button opens a form where you can assign a competency to one or more people at once — e.g. an STS course or medical certificate.

personnel-filters.title: Search, role and status
personnel-filters.description: Search by name or competency name, and filter by role/title and status. Red people have expired competencies affecting status.

personnel-card.title: Personnel card
personnel-card.description: Each card shows name, role, number of pending courses (if any), and a compact view of competencies. Red badges = expired, yellow = expiring within 30 days.

person-dialog.title: Person details
person-dialog.description: The detail view for a person shows all competencies, available courses, and lets you add new competencies directly.

person-logbok.title: Personal logbook
person-logbok.description: "Logbook" opens the person's flight logbook — all missions and flight hours logged for them.

person-competencies.title: Competencies
person-competencies.description: Each competency can be edited, deleted, downloaded (PDF), and you can control whether it "affects status" (red/yellow on expiry). Click a competency to edit type, name, dates and upload a document.

person-courses.title: Available courses
person-courses.description: Assigned courses and self-service courses (available to everyone) are shown here. Press "Take course" to start it directly from this dialog.

person-add-competency.title: Add competency to person
person-add-competency.description: The form at the bottom of the dialog lets you quickly add a new competency to this specific person — type, name, issue/expiry date and optional document.

add-competency.title: Assign competency to multiple
add-competency.description: This dialog is used when you want to assign the same competency to many people at once. Select type, name, dates and the people — one row is created per person.

done.title: You've seen the entire Resources module
done.description: Remember: green/yellow/red status is updated automatically based on competency expiry, maintenance deadlines, warnings and payload. Keep the lists clean for a living dashboard of your fleet.

startFlight.title: Start flight
startFlight.description: Learn how to start a flight from the dashboard — with checklists, missions, SafeSky publishing and DroneTag.

intro.title: Start a flight from the dashboard
intro.description: The "Start flight" button opens the dialog where you select a mission, complete checklists and decide the publishing mode before takeoff.

open-dialog.title: The Start flight dialog
open-dialog.description: Here we gather everything you need before takeoff: air traffic, checklists, mission, publishing and DroneTag device.

traffic.title: Nearby air traffic
traffic.description: AviSafe automatically checks the nearest manned traffic within 20 km. Red = under 5 km, yellow = under 15 km. Traffic above 5,000 ft is filtered out.

checklists.title: Pre-flight checklists
checklists.description: The company's required checklists must be completed before you can start. Click "Open checklist" to fill it in. Admin can attach new checklists.

mission.title: Select mission
mission.description: Link the flight to a planned mission. Missions with a route (📍 icon) automatically give access to SafeSky Advisory publishing.

publish-mode.title: Publishing mode
publish-mode.description: Choose whether the flight should be published to SafeSky: "None", "Advisory" (route notification) or "Live UAV" (real-time position via DroneTag). Live UAV is recommended for increased safety in shared airspace.

dronetag.title: DroneTag device
dronetag.description: For Live UAV you need to select a registered DroneTag device. It continuously sends position to SafeSky and other operators see you on the map.

submit.title: Ready for takeoff
submit.description: Press "Start flight" when everything is in place. The timer starts and the flight appears in Active flights on the dashboard.

uploadDroneLog.title: Upload DJI flight log
uploadDroneLog.description: Learn how to upload flight logs manually, process pending auto-sync logs and link them to missions.

intro.title: Upload flight log
intro.description: From the dashboard you'll find "Upload flight log" under the flight time menu. You can upload DJI and ArduPilot logs, or let AviSafe sync automatically from your DJI account.

open-dialog.title: Choose method
open-dialog.description: Two options: upload a file manually, or log in with your DJI account to fetch logs from the cloud automatically.

file.title: Upload file manually
file.description: Click here to select a TXT or ZIP file (or .bin for ArduPilot). You can also select multiple files at once for bulk upload.

dji.title: DJI account (auto-sync)
dji.description: Log in with DJI once and AviSafe will fetch new logs automatically in the background. Recommended for daily use.

pending.title: Pending logs to process
pending.description: Auto-synced logs appear here. Green ✓ = drone matched, yellow ⚠ = drone needs linking, red = error. The "Mine only" toggle filters to your logs.

match.title: Match drone, battery and mission
match.description: Select a log from the list to open details. Here you link the log to the correct drone/battery (create new if needed) and link it to a mission on the same day.

finish.title: Processed logs
finish.description: Once a log is processed, it moves to Statistics → Flight log, and battery, altitude and route data becomes available in the flight dashboard.

admin.title: Administration — full walkthrough
admin.description: In-depth tour of the admin page: users, customers, email, SORA, my company and training. Requires administrator access. Superadmin functions (Companies, NOTAM, Calculator) are not part of this tour.

intro.title: Welcome to administration
intro.description: The admin page is the control panel for your company. Here you approve users, manage roles and department affiliation, send invitations, edit email templates, define SORA limits, and keep departments and training organized. You must be an administrator to run this tour.

tabs.title: Tabs
tabs.description: The content is split into tabs: Users, Customers, Email, SORA (requires add-on), My company and Training. We'll go thoroughly through each tab. Some tabs may be hidden depending on subscription and add-on modules.

users-tab.title: Users — overview
users-tab.description: The main tab for user management. Here you find the registration code, send invitations, approve pending users and manage roles for approved users.

registration-code.title: Registration code
registration-code.description: The unique code employees enter when registering so they end up in your company. Press "Copy" to share it. Each department has its own code — check under "My company" for department codes.

invite.title: Invite new user
invite.description: Send an invitation email with the registration code and a link. If the company has multiple departments, you can choose which department the user should join before sending. The user gets a ready-made invitation and appears under "Pending" once the account is created.

pending.title: Pending approvals
pending.description: New users must be approved before they get access to the app. Press "Approve" to activate the account — or the trash icon to reject and delete. Each approved user increases the number of seats on the subscription, so remember to reject spam registrations.

approved-actions.title: Mailing list and bulk sending
approved-actions.description: The button row gives you Show mailing list (shows all emails in a text field) and Copy mailing list (copies all addresses comma-separated to the clipboard). Handy for newsletters or external communication tools.

approved-list.title: Approved users — cards
approved-list.description: The list of all active users in the company (and departments if you're a parent company). On desktop you see toggles directly in the row; on mobile you open the card to edit. Each user shows name, email and department badge.

user-roles-switches.title: Roles and toggles per user
user-roles-switches.description: For each user you control: Role (administrator/user), Department, Technical responsible (receives drone maintenance alerts), Can approve missions (with choice of which departments), Incident follow-up owner, and ECCAIRS access (if enabled). Changes take effect immediately via RLS.

user-training-delete.title: Training and deletion
user-training-delete.description: The "In training" toggle locks the user to only the modules you select via the Training picker — perfect for new hires. The Delete button permanently removes the user from Auth, but operational history is retained (missions, flight times, incidents are kept with the name anonymized).

tab-customers.title: Customers — tab
tab-customers.description: Register and manage external clients. These can be linked to missions and used as an internal POC across departments.

customers-add.title: Add new customer
customers-add.description: Use the "New customer" button at the top to register contact information, billing details and a default internal POC. Customers can be assigned responsible people who appear automatically on missions.

customers-list.title: Customer list and shared customers
customers-list.description: Click a customer to edit or archive it. If the company is a department under a parent company, you'll also see shared customers from the parent company marked with a badge — these are shared and can be used on your missions.

tab-email.title: Email — tab
tab-email.description: Here you edit email templates (welcome, approval, alerts), change sender settings and send bulk emails to users/customers.

email-templates.title: Email templates
email-templates.description: At the top you'll find all editable templates: welcome, approval, invitation, alerts etc. Click a template to edit the subject and content with variables like {{userName}} and {{companyName}}.

email-settings.title: Sender settings
email-settings.description: The "Email settings" button opens the dialog where you set sender name, reply-to address and optionally your own domain configuration. Default sender is noreply@avisafe.no via Resend.

email-bulk.title: Bulk sending and history
email-bulk.description: At the bottom you'll find the bulk email form: choose recipients (all users, all customers, or a custom list), write the subject and content, and send. The history below the form shows all previous campaigns with status and open statistics.

tab-sora.title: SORA settings
tab-sora.description: Requires the SORA add-on. Here you set company-specific defaults that the AI risk assessment and pilots build missions on.

sora-flightgeo.title: Default flight geography
sora-flightgeo.description: Define the default Flight Geography Area that auto-fills on new SORA missions (typically a meter radius around takeoff). The pilot can adjust per mission, but this is the starting point.

sora-altitude.title: Altitude limits
sora-altitude.description: Set the company's default max AGL altitude. Used both as an auto-fill value and as a threshold in risk assessment — if the limit is exceeded, the mission is flagged for extra review.

sora-mitigations.title: Mitigations and standards
sora-mitigations.description: Pre-selected mitigations (M1/M2 measures, procedures) that appear on all SORA missions. Reduces manual work for the pilot and ensures company standards are followed.

tab-child.title: My company — tab
tab-child.description: Company setup: name, terminology, departments/subsidiaries, checklists, integrations and control over which settings propagate down to departments.

child-info.title: Company info and terminology
child-info.description: Edit name, logo and terminology — drone operator vs. airline. Terminology changes wording throughout the app (e.g. "pilot" vs. "master").

child-departments.title: Departments / subsidiaries
child-departments.description: Create underlying departments with their own registration code. Each department gets isolated data via RLS, but the parent company sees everything via the hierarchical view. Users can belong to one department at a time.

child-checklists.title: Default checklists
child-checklists.description: Edit default checklists for pre-flight, post-flight and maintenance. These act as templates for all missions and resources in the company — the pilot can add mission-specific items along the way.

child-integrations-propagation.title: Integrations and propagation
child-integrations-propagation.description: Connect FlightHub 2, ECCAIRS and DroneTag with tokens (encrypted in the database). Further down you control granular propagation: each setting type (checklists, customers, email templates …) can be toggled in/out for each department.

tab-training.title: Training — tab
tab-training.description: Course builder and assignment. Create courses (manually or with AI), assign to users, track status and unlock modules based on passed courses.

training-courses.title: Course builder (manual)
training-courses.description: Build courses as a sequence of modules: video (YouTube/Vimeo), text (rich formatting), PDF slides, and guided tours that point directly into the app. Set the passing score requirement, number of attempts and which modules the course unlocks on completion.

training-ai.title: AI course generator
training-ai.description: "Generate with AI" builds a complete course from a topic and target audience — it suggests structure, finds relevant YouTube clips, writes text and creates a quiz. You can edit everything afterwards before publishing.

training-assign.title: Assignment
training-assign.description: Assign courses to individuals or entire departments at once. Set a completion deadline; the user gets a notification and sees the course under "My courses" on the profile page.

training-status.title: Status and score
training-status.description: The Status tab shows all ongoing and completed assignments with score, number of attempts and time spent. Passed courses automatically unlock modules in the app for the user.

done.title: You've seen the admin page
done.description: Remember: roles and approvals here immediately affect access throughout the app via RLS. The Delete button permanently removes the user from Auth, but keeps operational history (missions, flight times, incidents) for audit purposes. Need to reopen the tour later? You'll find it under "Guided tour" in the menu.
